title: Scheduler journal hotfix R1 — bound SSE reads, converge idle cohorts to silence, clear stale backoff on fresh canonical wakes (live-ops regression)
description: Live-ops fix for sustained CPU burn + dashboard latency (events table 161k rows, ~1.2 cores idle), plus R1 audit corrections. R0: (1) eventsSince pages 'WHERE seq > ? ORDER BY seq LIMIT ?' via store.listEventsSince — bounded rows, per-row hash verification preserved, latest_seq = high-water delivered so truncated pages let SSE clients continue paging. (2) settle() adds wait_streak: consecutive timed-wait outcomes that leave no pending generation scale next_due by min(2^streak,12) (300s → ~1h ceiling); pending work or non-timed outcomes reset it. R1-F1: observe() and accountWake() post-dedup writes now reset next_due=null + wait_streak=0 — a genuinely new verified wake/observation creates new pending work and must not inherit a stale no-progress checkpoint (previously NOT_DUE_YET could hold fresh work up to ~1h); settle() clears next_due when pending work remains after a pass. Duplicate wakes/no-op observations/markDue scheduler polling do NOT reset backoff (dedup early-returns unchanged). R1-F2: nextFairCandidate pages through the remaining cohort in-call (SCAN_PAGES=3 → ≤191 rows fully scanned per call, sized to the proof read budget with lease reads only for queue-actionable rows) — a completely scanned unchanged cohort converges to zero commits instead of alternating FAIR_VISIT/FAIR_ROUND; larger unchanged cohorts emit at most one cursor-progress commit per call. FAIR_VISIT on usable finds, FAIR_ROUND on bound refresh/wrap, deterministic rank order, claim re-proof under the writer lock, and B06 cohort-refresh semantics preserved; new registrations remain discoverable via bound-refresh commits. Evidence: 9 hotfix tests, failing-first on committed HEAD (H4 stale next_due carried; H5 4 commits/sweep at cohorts 64/65/128), all green post-fix; adjacent suites 236/236; tsc clean; build green.
